(a) If you’re looking for something with the driving force to push you through that last rep, you might crank up some high-BPM anthems—think Survivor’s ‘Eye of the Tiger,’ Queen’s ‘Don’t Stop Me Now,’ and The Prodigy’s ‘Firestarter.’ The relentless beats and bold choruses can give your workout an unstoppable momentum.
(b) If you’re looking for something with the driving force to push you through that last rep, you might crank up some classic heavy metal—think Judas Priest’s ‘Electric Eye,’ Iron Maiden’s ‘Aces High,’ and early Metallica tracks like ‘Seek & Destroy.’ The galloping riffs and relentless drums can give your workout the same raw energy as the picket lines in the stories you love to explore.
(c) If you’re looking for something with the driving force to push you through that last rep, you might crank up some high-energy salsa music—think Willie Colón’s ‘Idilio,’ Celia Cruz’s ‘Quimbara,’ and El Gran Combo’s ‘Brujeria.’ The vibrant percussion and layered rhythms can give your workout a lively, dance-floor intensity.
(d) If you’re looking for something with the driving force to push you through that last rep, you might crank up some spirited Celtic folk rock—think The Pogues’ ‘If I Should Fall from Grace with God,’ The Corrs’ ‘Toss the Feathers,’ and Dropkick Murphys’ ‘I’m Shipping Up to Boston.’ The blend of traditional melodies and modern drive can give your workout an energizing, rootsy edge.

4. **Micro-breaks in editing**: Set an alarm to pause every hour. Stand, look away from screens, and physically shift your environment.

5. **Delegate or stagger research tasks** when possible — share fact-checking with collaborators so you don’t carry every detail alone.
